task: ADR-style design decision. The daemon's `yakos.term.create` RPC registers an externally-owned terminal session and must record an owner. Two options: (A) keep deriving the owner server-side from the loopbackowner package (file-persisted ID, socket is mode 0600 owner-UID); (B) reuse the networked-console authsession so every RPC carries a user session and the owner is the authenticated user. Read cli-go/internal/serve/term_methods.go, cli-go/internal/loopbackowner/loopbackowner.go and skim cli-go/internal/authsession. Recommend A or B for today's single-user loopback deployment and say what would have to change to make B the right answer later. Write it as a short ADR: Context, Decision, Consequences. Cite files. This is a read-only task: do not edit, write, or create any file.
expected_outcomes: Picks a single option (A recommended for the single-user loopback path) rather than listing both without a decision
Grounds the decision in the code: term_methods.go derives the owner via loopbackowner and does not accept an owner from RPC params
Names the threat: an owner taken from caller-supplied params could be forged by a hostile local caller; the UID-restricted 0600 socket plus server-side derivation avoids that
States a concrete trigger for revisiting (for example the RPC surface becoming reachable by multiple authenticated users or over the network)
Uses ADR structure Context / Decision / Consequences and cites real file paths only
